newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse shrugs off tax hikes by the close.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse shrugs off tax hikes by the close.

text.p: French shares finished slightly lower on Monday after the government announced widely anticipated increases in corporate taxes to enable France to reduce its budget deficit and qualify for European monetary union.
The CAC-40 blue-chip index closed down 2.57 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2,874.12 after recovering from an early low of 2,830.68.
The CAC-40 July futures contract fell one point to 2,857.
The broader SBF120 index finished down 4.98 at 1,968.64.
Volume was a moderate 7.08 billion francs.

Brokers said the CAC index, which lost 2.21 percent on Friday in anticipation of corporate tax hikes, was helped by Wall Street's recovery from its early lows and the fact that tax on share sales would not be raised along with other corporate taxes.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told a news conference that a government-ordered audit of France's finances showed the public deficit running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of this year's estimated gross domestic product -- well above the three percent target set in the Maastricht treaty for monetary union.
He announced plans to cut the deficit by 32 billion francs, with 22 billion generated by higher taxes on corporate profits and capital gains.
The bond market finished a trace weaker in line with German bond prices, while the franc firmed.
"The impact on the markets was mitigated because 80 percent of what was announced today was known," said economist Jean-Louis Mourier at Louis Dreyfus Finance.

Retail and consumer goods stocks rose on investor relief that the government did not raise taxes on households. Pen and lighter manufacturer Bic rose 1.61 percent to 945 francs. Carrefour rose 0.54 percent, Promodes gained 1.1 percent and Pinault-Printemps added 3.55 percent. Its Redoute branch bought a mail order company.
* Assurances Generales de France fell 2.46 percent after the government said on Friday it would privatise insurer GAN, in which AGF has expressed interest.
